newsitem.title: UK: NWE GAS OIL STABLE, INACTIVE AS AUG EXPIRES.
newsitem.headline: NWE GAS OIL STABLE, INACTIVE AS AUG EXPIRES.

text.p: NWE gas oil was stable but inactive on Tuesday with most players concentrating on the expiry of the front month IPE August contract, traders said.
August last traded at $168.50 a tonne, up 50 cents, before going off the board. September IPE was trading $1 firmer at $170.75.
Traders saw further grounds for early caution in the publication due this afternoon of July European oil stock data.
In June middle distillate stocks in the 15 countries of the European Union plus Norway were 15.15 million barrels or 5.1 percent higher than in June 1996.

On the barge market Rotterdam refinery heating oil was offered at September IPE flat and assessed against the August contract at a $1/1.50 premium. On Friday a Wall Street trader was rumoured to have sold some 30,000 tonnes of heating oil in barges at around August IPE flat ex-Antwerp.
Low sulphur diesel was assessed at September IPE +$3.50/$4.00 fob ARA.
German heating oil was seen around September +$0.75/$1.50 for second half August. Low sulphur diesel was bid at September IPE +$4.50 and offered up to a $6 premium.
